records.assessment: BC Hydro reported storm damage.
records.rationale: The utility described new outages amid high winds and ongoing repairs. It did not separately address a possible cyber cause.
records.impactNote: Electricity service was interrupted in the Central Interior. BC Hydro did not give a separate customer count for the November 11 storm.

records.title: Substation failure cuts power in Albany and Bethlehem
records.summary: About 6,800 National Grid customers lost power. Traffic lights in Albany went dark, and the city reported problems at sewage pump stations.
records.cause: National Grid identified an equipment failure at its New Krumkill substation in New York.
records.assessment: National Grid cited a substation equipment failure.
records.rationale: Spokesman Patrick Stella described an equipment failure and repairs. His reported statement did not address cyber involvement.
records.impactNote: Power was out for about 6,800 customers across Albany and Bethlehem. Nearly all had service back by 10:30 a.m. Eastern.

records.title: Backup test interrupts payroll and timekeeping access
records.summary: Employees at affected organizations could not sign in to Workday to clock in, check pay or finish benefits enrollment. Washington University told staff to record hours manually.
records.impactNote: Workday reported disruption in two data centers. Recovery times varied by customer.
records.cause: During a backup test, services at Workday’s disaster-recovery site connected to production databases. Workday paused affected systems to reconcile the data.
records.assessment: Workday ruled out a cybersecurity incident in a statement reported by ABC10.
records.rationale: ABC10 reported Workday’s statement after service was restored. Earlier that morning PCgeek attributed the disruption to the test while cautioning that the reporting available at that point could not rule out an attack.

history.text: At 7:05 p.m. Central on Friday, Washington University relayed Workday’s notice about the backup test and the pause in production service.
PCgeek attributed the disruption to the backup test on the available evidence, while cautioning that no full root-cause report had appeared.
ABC10 published Workday’s denial and its statement that the outage affected two data centers.
UC Today reported that a Workday spokesperson ruled out a cybersecurity incident and said service had been restored by 11 a.m. Eastern.

records.title: Sign-in and connectivity fail in AWS’s Northern Virginia region
records.summary: Customers had trouble signing in to the AWS console, registering accounts and connecting to some services. A subset of network load balancers took more than three hours to recover.
records.cause: AWS identified authentication and network failures. Its recovery notice did not give a root cause.
records.assessment: Two security publications found no indication of an attack in the public AWS updates.
records.rationale: SecurTek reviewed AWS’s notices and described a service disruption with no indication of malicious activity. Cyber Security News reached a similar assessment. AWS confirmed the outage and its recovery.
records.impactNote: The outage affected customers in the US-EAST-1 region, including some Kiro and Amazon Connect users.
